glucuronide, N1627 -250 mg, Sigma Aldrich). The total reaction volume was 250 μL. The compound dissolved in DMSO (100%), which becomes 2% in the ultimate assay (250 μL) and the similar conditions were used for standard (D-saccharic acid 1, 4-lactone, Sigma Aldrich). The reaction mixture contained 185 μL of 0.1 M acetate buffer, 5 μL of test compound solution, 10 μL of (1U) enzyme solution (G7396 -25KU, Sigma Aldrich) was incubated at 37°C for 30 min. steps.title: Create individual pharmacophore models
steps.instruction: Generate 2‑D and 3‑D structure‑based pharmacophore models for each of the three β‑glucuronidase crystal structures (PDB IDs 3LPF, 3LPG and 3K4D) using LigandScout version 3.0.

substeps.instruction: Open LigandScout 3.0 and load PDB ID 3LPF; double‑click the highlighted yellow box and select “Generate the pharmacophore feature” from the upper toolbar; the software will display the 2‑D and 3‑D pharmacophore model in the middle and right panes.
Repeat the same procedure for PDB ID 3LPG.
Repeat the same procedure for PDB ID 3K4D.

steps.title: Build shared and merged pharmacophores
steps.instruction: Create a five‑element shared‑feature pharmacophore model and a merged‑feature model by aligning the three individual models.

substeps.instruction: Choose the 3LPF model as the reference because its bound inhibitor has an IC₅₀ of 326 nM.
Align the 3LPG and 3K4D models onto the 3LPF reference.
Generate the shared‑feature five‑element model.
Generate the merged‑feature model that contains all pharmacophore features from the three individual models.

steps.title: Filter chemical database
steps.instruction: Apply Lipinski’s rule of five to the in‑house chemical library using MOE and retain only drug‑like compounds.

substeps.instruction: Load the full database into MOE (2010‑212).
Filter out any compound that violates Lipinski ROF criteria.
After filtration, 8 262 drug‑like candidates remain; save the filtered library as an MOE database file (.mdb).

steps.title: Export pharmacophore models
steps.instruction: Save each of the five pharmacophore models (three individual, one shared, one merged) in MOE‑compatible .ph4 format.

steps.title: Virtual screening with pharmacophores
steps.instruction: Search the 8 262 filtered compounds against the five pharmacophore models in MOE to identify hits.

substeps.instruction: Load the .ph4 pharmacophore files and the .mdb compound library into MOE.
Run the pharmacophore‑based virtual screening (scaffold hopping) for each model.
Collect all retrieved compounds; a total of 1 249 hits are obtained.

steps.title: Prepare receptor for docking
steps.instruction: Set up the β‑glucuronidase structure (PDB 3LPF) for docking in the chosen software.

substeps.instruction: Download PDB ID 3LPF (resolution 2.26 Å) which contains the Z77 thiourea‑derivative ligand.
Select chain A of the homodimer and retain conserved water molecules HOH 655 and HOH 733.
Note catalytic triad residues Glu540, Glu451 and Tyr504, plus additional interacting residues Glu413A, Leu361, Phe448A and Tyr472.

steps.title: Prepare ligand set
steps.instruction: Convert and minimize all ligands before docking.

substeps.instruction: Take the 66 literature‑reported β‑glucuronidase inhibitors (provided as 2‑D .mol files) and convert each to 3‑D .mol2 format using the Open Babel command‑line on Linux.
Minimize the resulting 3‑D structures with SYBYL (Tripos) to generate low‑energy conformers.
Combine these 66 minimized inhibitors with the 1 249 virtual‑screening hits to form the final docking library.

steps.title: Dock ligands with FRED
steps.instruction: Perform molecular docking of the 1 249 hits and the 66 known inhibitors against the prepared 3LPF receptor using FRED.

steps.title: Rescore docking results
steps.instruction: Re‑evaluate FRED docking scores with GOLD 5.1 using multiple scoring functions and calculate enrichment factors.

substeps.instruction: Import the FRED docking poses into GOLD 5.1.
Score each pose with Gold‑score, Chem‑score and ASP (Astex Statistical Potential).
For each scoring function, compute enrichment factors at the top 5 %, 10 %, 15 % and 20 % of the ranked list using the formula: Enrichment = (Hits / Ns) ÷ (Ht / Nt).
Record that Chemgauss‑4 (the FRED default) performed best at 5 % enrichment, while Chem‑score was superior at 10 %, 15 % and 20 %.

steps.title: MTT cytotoxicity assay
steps.instruction: Determine the cytotoxicity of selected compounds on 3T3 cells using an MTT assay.

substeps.instruction: Remove existing medium from each well and add 200 µL fresh culture medium containing the test compound at concentrations ranging from 1 µM to 30 µM.
Incubate the cells for 48 h at 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.
Add 200 µL of MTT solution (0.5 mg · mL⁻¹) to each well and incubate for an additional 4 h.
Add 100 µL DMSO to each well to solubilize formazan crystals.
Measure absorbance at 540 nm using a microplate reader (SpectraMax Plus, Molecular Devices).
Calculate percent inhibition: % inhibition = 100 − [(OD_test − OD_negative) / (OD_positive − OD_negative) × 100].
Determine the IC₅₀ (concentration causing 50 % growth inhibition) for each compound.
